title: NDT Report Review in Pascagoula, MS | Refinery and Fabrication
description: Remote, independent review of refinery turnaround, tank and fabrication NDT reports and digital inspection data from Pascagoula and Jackson County.
h1: Pascagoula refinery and fabrication records, checked by an independent NDT reviewer
intro: Jackson County packs a very large refinery, an LNG terminal, heavy fabrication and a deep-water port into a short stretch of the Mississippi coast. Together they generate turnaround packages, tank inspection files, piping circuit histories and weld records from fabrication bays, most of it now in digital form. When an owner, a contractor or a buyer needs someone outside the job to say whether those NDT reports actually prove what they claim, that is the work we do. There is no Atlantis presence in Pascagoula or Moss Point: every review runs remotely from Houston and Hyderabad on the files sent to us.

highlights.h: Turnaround packages closed out on evidence
highlights.p: Shutdown work leaves hundreds of reports to accept in a short window. An outside reviewer can sample them against the inspection plan and flag the ones that would not survive an audit before the unit restarts.

highlights.h: Tank and piping histories that hang together
highlights.p: Thickness data only means something when this year's readings sit on the same locations as last year's. We check that the record keeps that continuity.

highlights.h: Shop weld records read against the right code
highlights.p: Coast fabricators often work to several codes at once. The review starts from the purchase order, not from the code the technician usually uses.

sections.h: What the Jackson County coast produces in inspection records
p: Pascagoula's industry is organised around two harbours run by the Jackson County Port Authority. On the east bank, the Bayou Casotte terminal lists Chevron, Gulf LNG and Bollinger Shipyards among its tenants; on the west bank, the Pascagoula River terminal serves Ingalls Shipbuilding alongside the public berths. Each tenant type leaves a different trail of NDT paperwork, and a reviewer needs to know which trail a package belongs to before reading it.
The table is a guide to the area and the records it typically generates. The facilities are named to describe the industrial base, not as clients, and naming them implies no review of their records.

sections.h: The refinery and why its records carry weight
p: Chevron's Pascagoula Refinery, which began operating in 1963, is described in the company's 2024 fact sheet as its largest US refinery, with crude capacity of about 369,000 barrels a day and more than ninety per cent of Mississippi's refining capacity. It produces gasoline, jet fuel, diesel, base oil and other products. A plant of that size is covered by OSHA's process safety management standard, whose mechanical integrity element expects inspection and testing of process equipment to follow recognised and generally accepted good engineering practice, with the results documented.

In practice that means API 510 for pressure vessels, API 570 for process piping and API 653 for aboveground storage tanks, with ASME Section VIII and ASME B31.3 governing repairs and new construction. Every one of those documents assumes that the inspection data is trustworthy. If the thickness reading was taken at the wrong location, if the technician's certificate had lapsed, or if a crack indication was dispositioned against the wrong acceptance table, the interval and the repair decision built on that report rest on sand. The review exists to test that foundation.

sections.h: Turnaround close-out: what a sample review finds
p: A turnaround compresses months of inspection into weeks, often with several contractors working at once. By the time the unit is ready to start up, the owner's inspection group is holding a stack of reports that must be accepted into the plant's records. An independent report review at that point usually samples across contractors and methods, weighted towards the circuits and vessels the risk ranking cares most about.

The findings tend to cluster. Reports that cite a procedure revision the contractor never submitted to the owner. Thickness readings recorded without condition monitoring location identifiers, so they cannot be trended. Magnetic particle reports that do not say whether the surface was cleaned to bare metal or whether a wet or dry technique was used. Repair weld records showing the final examination but not the examination of the excavation before welding. None of these necessarily means the equipment is unsafe, but each weakens the record the next inspector will depend on.

Timing matters as much as content. Once a unit is back on line, a gap in an internal vessel report can only be closed at the next shutdown, which may be years away. A review run while scaffolding is still standing gives the owner the option of sending a technician back to repeat or complete an examination, rather than carrying a weak record into the next interval and explaining it to an auditor later. That is why we suggest agreeing the sample and the file transfer before the turnaround starts, so reports can be read in batches as contractors submit them.
list: Reports matched to the owner's inspection plan item by item, so nothing planned goes unreported
Procedure numbers and revisions checked against the procedures the owner actually approved
Technician qualification confirmed for the method, the level and the date of the examination
Thickness data checked for location identifiers that link it to earlier surveys
Every rejectable indication followed through to repair, re-examination and acceptance

sections.h: Storage tanks: floor maps, shell data and the API 653 report
p: Tank inspection packages from refineries and terminals combine several kinds of evidence: magnetic flux leakage or ultrasonic floor scan results, prove-up ultrasonic readings on the indications the scan found, shell thickness measurements, weld inspections on repaired plates and the authorised inspector's own report. The reviewer checks that these agree with each other. A floor map that shows a deep indication with no prove-up reading beside it, or a prove-up reading that does not appear on the map, is a gap the owner needs closed before relying on the next inspection date.

We do not act as the API 653 authorised inspector, and we do not calculate remaining life or perform fitness-for-service work; those decisions stay with the owner's inspector and engineer. What we can say is whether the NDT data placed in front of them was gathered and reported well enough to support their judgement.

Heavy welding has a long history in Jackson County, and a supply base of steel shops, pipe fabricators and mechanical contractors serves the refinery, the LNG terminal and the other port tenants. Many inspectors and welders on this coast have worked under demanding weld quality regimes, and the reports they write for refinery and terminal clients often reflect several codes at once.

For fabrication records sent from the area, whether vessels, piping spools or structural steel, the review begins with the contract. A spool built to ASME B31.3 for the refinery, a frame built to AWS D1.1 and a vessel built to Section VIII each carry their own examination extent and acceptance criteria. We check that the weld map, the weld log and the NDT reports reconcile, that each repair was re-examined, and that the acceptance standard quoted is the one the contract invokes rather than the one the shop uses most.

sections.h: Mississippi regulators that shape the record
p: Boilers and pressure vessels in the state fall under the Boiler and Pressure Vessel Safety Act of 1974, administered by the Boiler & Pressure Vessel Safety Division of the Mississippi State Department of Health. State and private inspectors examine more than seventeen thousand boilers and pressure vessels a year under that program. Intrastate gas pipelines are overseen by the Pipeline Safety Division of the Mississippi Public Service Commission, while interstate pipelines answer to PHMSA. The refinery's process safety programme answers to OSHA.

Radiation is the other piece. Mississippi has been an NRC Agreement State since 1962, and the Division of Radiological Health within the State Department of Health licenses radioactive material in the state, including the sources industrial radiographers use. Atlantis does not take radiographs in Mississippi; reviewing the film, CR and DR images that an owner's licensed radiography contractor produced, including image quality and interpretation, is document review and is part of the service.

sections.h: Digital inspection data: what we open and what we look for
p: Most refinery inspection data now lives in an inspection data management system or a contractor's digital reporting platform before it ever becomes a PDF. For a review we ask for the underlying files wherever possible: corrosion mapping and phased array files, digital radiography images in their native format, thickness exports from the data logger, eddy current tube data and the configuration of the reporting template. Raw data lets the reviewer see what the instrument recorded rather than only what the report says it recorded.

Digital reporting brings its own failure modes. A template can carry yesterday's procedure number forward automatically. An electronic signature may be applied in bulk by an administrator rather than by the qualified interpreter. A thickness export may pass through a spreadsheet where readings are rounded, sorted or overwritten before they reach the report. An NDT data review traces the lineage from instrument file to final report, checks that settings match the qualified procedure, and confirms that the person whose name appears on the interpretation held the right certification on that day.

sections.h: Who leads the review and where its limits sit
p: Ultrasonic, radiographic, magnetic particle, penetrant and visual reviews are run by an ASNT NDT Level III whose certification covers exactly those five methods. Others on the review team come from nuclear, maritime, oil and gas and petrochemical work, a mix that suits a coast where refinery, terminal and heavy fabrication records sit side by side. For eddy current tube data or any method outside those five, the proposal names a reviewer certified as the contract requires.

Independence has a practical meaning here: we will not review a report on work that Atlantis examined. We do not act as inspector of record or as an Authorized Inspector for state-registered vessels, and we do not certify the technicians whose reports we read. The output is an opinion. Each report is classed as sound, deficient in documentation only, or deficient in disposition, and every finding points to the clause or procedure step and the record that supports it.

sections.h: From the first email to the written opinion
p: Send the reports, the procedures and specifications they rely on, and any raw digital files through the secure transfer link we provide. We read enough to define the work, then return the scope and a quote, setting out what will be sampled, what will be read in full and what questions remain open. Work starts on your acceptance, and clarifications go by email or video call; no one needs a gate pass or a site visit, and we reply within one business day when a new request comes in.

Typical Pascagoula requests include a second opinion on a contractor's rejected weld reports, a pre-audit check of a unit's piping thickness history, acceptance of a vendor's vessel data book, and a review of inspection records that come with equipment bought second-hand. Each ends in the same deliverable: a written opinion an inspection manager or quality lead can file, act on and defend.

faqs.q: Does Atlantis have people or premises in Pascagoula or Jackson County?
faqs.a: No. Atlantis's offices are in Houston and Hyderabad. Every Pascagoula review is carried out remotely on the records you send, without a site visit.

faqs.q: Can you review turnaround reports before a unit restarts?
faqs.a: Yes. We usually sample across contractors and methods, weighted towards the equipment your inspection plan ranks highest, and report which records need correcting before they enter the plant's history.

faqs.q: Do you review API 653 tank inspection packages?
faqs.a: We review the NDT evidence in them: floor scan maps, prove-up readings, shell thickness data and weld inspection reports. The authorised inspector's judgement and any remaining-life calculation stay with the owner's inspector and engineer.

faqs.q: Which agency inspects boilers and pressure vessels in Mississippi?
faqs.a: The Boiler & Pressure Vessel Safety Division of the Mississippi State Department of Health, alongside private inspectors, under the state's Boiler and Pressure Vessel Safety Act of 1974.

faqs.q: Can Atlantis radiograph welds at a Mississippi shop or plant?
faqs.a: No. We do not perform industrial radiography anywhere in the United States. We do review radiographs, CR and DR images taken by your licensed contractor, including image quality and the interpretation.

faqs.q: Our customer rejected our fabrication weld reports. Can you give an independent view?
faqs.a: Yes. We check the rejection against the code and the purchase order and separate gaps in documentation from genuine examination problems, so you have a clear basis for the conversation with your customer.

faqs.q: Can you check a piping thickness history before an audit?
faqs.a: Yes. We sample the circuits your plan ranks highest and check that readings carry CML identifiers, that the gauge and calibration are recorded, and that each survey lines up with the last, so the corrosion rates your engineer calculates rest on consistent data.

faqs.q: What should we send to get started?
faqs.a: The reports, the procedures and specifications they cite and any raw digital inspection files. We come back with the scope and a quote, and we reply within one business day.
